cost: hex O(n) output 2n; encode O(n) output n..3n UTF-8 bytes; download streaming O(B) and 64 KiB buffer plus hashes. text retains full body. sleep/HTTP/filesystem/df costs external.
description: Polite gates each GET by elapsed time, returns nested transport/status results, reads text lossily or downloads through .part with content-length/stream cap, rolling hashes, sync and rename. Helpers hex/encode/civil/free_bytes project bytes, time and df output.
forward: Polite gates each GET by elapsed time, returns nested transport/status results, reads text lossily or downloads through .part with content-length/stream cap, rolling hashes, sync and rename. Helpers hex/encode/civil/free_bytes project bytes, time and df output.
inverse: Known Content-Length>limit cannot create the .part file. Stream overflow cannot return Fetched. Non-2xx cannot be silently retried inside Polite. Network and filesystem failure paths are source-derived, not exercised.

hex has unique byte inverse on even lowercase hex strings; encode is injective on UTF-8 bytes with canonical percent escapes. Lossy UTF-8 text has many compatible raw byte antecedents; Fetched metadata cannot reconstruct response body uniquely.
limitations: No network/DNS/download, real catalog/corpus/model/teacher or database execution. Effect paths are source-derived; finite helper tests are not universal verification. No executable percentage surrogate or speed claim; future caps require metric/domain/reference and remain 1/2/5/10%.
state: Status bodies are capped at 4096 bytes; text bodies have no cap. download succeeds only after bytes<=limit, sync and rename. Error cleanup and pacing reset are branch-specific, not uniformly guaranteed.
